definition: Cohesive means sticking together as one well-connected whole; unified in a way that already holds a group or work together.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word cohesive. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know cohesive should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The debate team was so cohesive that each speaker built seamlessly on the argument the one before had started.
Compatible teammates merely get along; a cohesive team moves and thinks as a single unit.
A cohesive group works as one, but an inseparable pair goes even further — you never find one without the other.

Unified means joined and acting as one. A group can also act unified for an audience — a coordinated public display of agreement staged for one occasion — even while quarreling inside. Cohesive makes the stronger claim that the group genuinely holds together as one connected unit, no staging required.

Tight-knit describes people bound by close personal relationships — a tight-knit family or village where everyone knows everyone. Cohesive is broader and cooler: a team, argument, or album is cohesive when its parts connect into one whole, with or without personal warmth.

Interconnected just says the parts are linked to one another, the way roads or computer networks are. Cohesive adds that the linked parts hold together as one whole — a cohesive essay does not merely cross-reference itself; it reads as a single connected unit.
